reply_acts.author: claude-2
reply_acts.text: (why it slides) The drawing is 2.84 times as wide as it is tall, and the figure in the page already takes about 79% of the window's width. A box at 80% that showed the whole drawing would be about 2% larger, which is no gain. So in the box the drawing takes the box's height instead. At 1600 by 900 that makes it 2046 px wide against 1260 in the page, about 1.6 times larger and close to its natural size. Since it is then wider than the box, it slides left and right as the pointer moves across. Nothing scrolls and the wheel is not involved.

reply_acts.author: claude-2
reply_acts.text:
("leaving a 20% margin, so mouse-away to the margin can exit") I took this as 10% on each side, so the box is at most 80% of the window's width and height.
- **To open:** rest the pointer on the figure for 200 ms. A quick pass across it while moving down the page does not open it.
- **To close:** move the pointer out to the margin, click in the margin, or press Escape.
- **No reopen loop:** if the pointer is over the figure's place in the page when the box closes, it stays closed until the pointer has left the figure.
- **Touch and narrow windows:** phones, and windows under 761 px wide, keep the plain figure.
- **Caption:** I added one sentence telling a reader how to enlarge it and put it back. Reword it as you like.

reply_acts.author: claude-2
claude-2
reply_acts.text:
(two things you may notice)
- **Aiming:** because the drawing slides as you move, a box shifts a little as you approach it. In my automated click test the click landed on the neighbouring box, SCAN, when I aimed at R16 from stale coordinates. By eye this should be easy to follow, but if it feels slippery, the alternative is to slide only while the pointer is near the left or right edge.
- **Other screen sizes:** I tested one size. The box height is capped at 870 px, so on a very large screen the drawing stops growing at 1.2 times its natural size.

reply_acts.text: (to try it) Push, then hard-reload the About page once (Ctrl+Shift+R). The frame's address has a new version, so the hard reload should only be needed for the About page itself.

previous_reply_acts.text: ("maybe I overwrote your changes?") You did not overwrite it: the fix is in the file the site serves, and a fresh browser shows the whole figure. Your browser is most likely still using its cached copy of the old `harness.html`. The notebook is republished.

("The published figure is still not full-size for me")
- **Git:** my commit `9d3762c` is under your `c76ffda` on `origin/master`.
- **Live file:** `https://hyperreal.enterprises/harness.html` contains the new sizing rule and was last modified at 19:12 UTC.
- **Fresh browser:** a headless Chromium screenshot of the live About page at 1600 px wide shows the whole figure, all six columns, the lower band and the purple boundary.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-2
previous_reply_acts.text: (why you still see the old one) The server sends no cache instruction for `harness.html`, so a browser that loaded the old version keeps reusing it for a few hours without asking again. Reloading the About page does not always reload the page inside the frame.
